A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MARVEL-40M+ and MARVEL-FX3D. Their main text, tables, figures, equations, and complete supplements are readable, and relocated or renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original annotation evaluations, a human study of text-to-3D generation, semantic-retention measurements, and qualitative results.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds a comparison of pretrained, Cap3D-fine-tuned, and MARVEL-fine-tuned generation, plus additional qualitative cases.

M1.justification: The annotation stages, component models, five-level hierarchy, and SD 3.5/DIS/SF3D generation pipeline are retained. Added explanations clarify existing procedures; the camera-elevation revision is a rendering setting rather than a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Section 9.4 and Figure 22 add explicit qualitative evaluation of simple and textureless objects, including inputs lacking texture cues. This is a limited test-scenario extension; the dataset families and principal annotation and generation tasks remain unchanged.

E2.justification: v2 Table 5 adds generation controls using pretrained SD 3.5 and SD 3.5 fine-tuned on Cap3D within MARVEL-FX3D. Cap3D previously participated in caption comparisons, but this downstream comparison is new. Existing caption and generation baselines remain.

E3.justification: Section 3.1 changes the reported rendering elevation from 60 to 30. ShapeNet and Pix3D sample counts change from 51,209 and 735 to 52,472 and 374. New fine-tuning controls reuse the stated 50-sample human-evaluation design. These revisions do not establish that earlier experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds a focused training-data/fine-tuning ablation in Table 5, four simple/textureless qualitative cases in Figure 22, and an estimated cost/throughput analysis in Table 7. Existing metadata and semantic-retention analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Five-person evaluation and scores reported with ± values already appear in v1. v2 extends this reporting format to new controls without introducing new run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical tests.

E6.justification: Existing Tables 2–4 retain their scores. New Table 5 reports prompt fidelity of 2.58, 6.54, and 7.71 for pretrained, Cap3D-fine-tuned, and MARVEL-fine-tuned variants. Table 7 adds estimated annotation costs, and Figure 22 adds qualitative outcomes. Table 1 revises totals from 8,901,201 to 8,902,103 objects and 44,506,005 to 44,510,515 captions.

T1.justification: Neither version develops new theoretical results or proofs. v2 Section 9.7 and Algorithm 1 explain the existing MTLD metric with pseudocode and examples; they do not introduce a new metric or mathematical result.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same claims about dataset scale, metadata-assisted annotation, five description levels, and rapid text-to-3D generation. The shortened conclusion and additional supporting comparisons do not materially redefine those contributions.

C2.justification: New appendix discussion explains handling of simple/textureless objects and argues that predefined annotation levels reduce repeated prompting, latency, and semantic drift. Section 8.3 introduces the qualification that MARVEL is estimated to cost less than Cap3D while having lower throughput. Existing failure limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-page link, unit-bounding-box normalization and camera-distance clarification, identification of Level 4 test captions, compute-cost assumptions, and MTLD pseudocode. Baseline training details in Section 10.2 were already documented in v1 Section 4.2.

R1.justification: The cited research set and Related Work section remain essentially unchanged. v2 adds an explicit contrast with separate view-processing/aggregation pipelines and refines its positioning against Cap3D through the new cost-versus-throughput comparison.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording edits, condenses the limitations and conclusion, expands acknowledgements and appendix explanations, and relocates baseline implementation details. The main narrative and section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 5 and 7, Algorithm 1, and Figure 22, with local layout reflow. Figure 2 changes the Level 5 label to Concise Tags, and Figure 3 clarifies its color legend. The semantic-retention table and final generation figures are retained with new numbering.

improvement.justification: The new within-pipeline comparison in Table 5 better supports the downstream value of MARVEL captions, while rendering, metric, and cost documentation improve transparency. These are focused gains: the cost comparison relies on estimates, and the additional robustness support consists of illustrative cases rather than a systematic evaluation.
